fact: HRV is the most reliable non-invasive marker of autonomic nervous system balance and recovery status
practical_application: Track HRV daily; use 7-day rolling average as baseline
relevance_to_achyut: High — monitor recovery with potential sleep issues

fact: HRV-guided training auto-regulation outperforms fixed programming for fitness improvements
practical_application: Reduce intensity on low-HRV days, push on high-HRV days

fact: HRV trends relative to YOUR baseline matter more than absolute values
A single night of alcohol can suppress HRV for up to 5 days
practical_application: Don't schedule heavy training within 48h of drinking

fact: Sleep consistency (same bed/wake times) matters as much as duration for recovery
Deep sleep (first half of night) is when growth hormone and muscle recovery peak
practical_application: Protect first 4 hours: no alcohol, screens, or heavy meals

fact: Modern wearables are 80-99% accurate for sleep/wake, 60-90% for sleep staging
practical_application: Good enough for trend tracking — don't obsess over exact minutes

fact: Composite readiness scores combine HRV, RHR, sleep, and respiratory rate for actionable guidance
practical_application: Green = planned session, red = deload or active recovery

fact: Sustained RHR increase of 5+ bpm for 3+ days often precedes illness or overtraining
practical_application: Track morning RHR; take deload if 5+ bpm above baseline

fact: CGMs reveal that individual glucose responses to identical foods vary enormously
practical_application: Use 2-week CGM period to identify personal trigger foods

fact: 10-15 min post-meal walks reduce glucose spikes by 30-50%
practical_application: Walk after largest meals — highest-ROI free metabolic intervention
relevance_to_achyut: High — easy, free, powerful at BMI 40

fact: Free phone apps (HRV4Training, Elite HRV) provide 80% of expensive wearable benefit
practical_application: Start with free tools; tracking habit matters more than precision
